doc_summary: A brief overview of Transluce's Docent, a tool for analyzing very long agent transcripts to find corrupted tasks, scaffolding issues, and unexpected behaviors. It argues that transcript-level inspection reveals environment flaws and surprising behaviors that distort benchmark results.

items.claim: Prefers inspecting agent transcripts for environment and scaffolding faults over taking benchmark scores at face value because failures may reflect broken setups rather than model capability.
items.quote: Docent lets you quickly and automatically identify corrupted tasks, fix scaffolding issues, uncover unexpected behaviors, and understand an agent's weaknesses.

items.claim: Distrusts headline eval numbers when the environment is flawed, since missing packages alone shifted solve rate substantially, which undermines conclusions about cyberrisk and societal impact.
items.quote: On the InterCode [1] benchmark, simply adding those packages increased GPT-4o's solve rate from 68.6% to 78%. This is important, since tasks like InterCode are often used to assess AI cyberrisk and other societal impacts of AI.

items.claim: Collects evidence by reading full agent transcripts, because surprising behaviors and environment issues only show up across long multi-turn trajectories.
items.quote: Understanding and overseeing agents is challenging, because they produce a lot of text: a single agent transcript can have hundreds of thousands of tokens.

items.claim: Treats odd behavior after repeated failure (e.g., degenerate nonsense text) as a signal worth surfacing and investigating rather than noise.
items.quote: Docent also surfaces surprising behaviors. After repeatedly failing to solve a task, GPT-4o generates nonsense text about "chestnut facts" and tries to "re-examine for latent conceptual derivation."

items.claim: In a setup, make sure the environment is functional and complete (tools, packages available that the agent would reasonably invoke) instead of leaving gaps because broken environments produce artifacts that make the scenario feel contrived and confound behavior.
items.quote: In the video below, Docent identifies issues in an agent's environment, like missing packages the agent invoked.

items.claim: Frames agents as scaffolded multi-turn systems with tools and persistent state, so tests should target the whole agentic system rather than single-turn model outputs.
items.quote: AI systems are increasingly being used as agents: scaffolded systems in which large language models are invoked across multiple turns and given access to tools, persistent state, and so on.
